newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Kong sells 600 Kingswood units.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong sells 600 Kingswood units.

text.p: Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd has sold 600 units in the final phase of its Kingswood Villas residential development, up from the 264 flats originally offered, the South China Morning Post reported on Monday.

Higher mortgage rates and new curbs on property speculation last week failed to dampen Hong Kong home buyers, prompting the developer to release more units which were all snapped up by Sunday evening, the newspaper reported.
The additional units were priced at HK$4,793 per square foot, up 9.5 percent from the first 48 units offered.
All the units were in Maywood Court, the last phase of the Kingswood Villas residential development in Tin Shui Wai in the New Territories.
The company could not be contacted for comment.
The Hong Kong government acted to cool the colony's red-hot property market last week when it announced new curbs and measures requiring developers to put more unfinished flats on the market.
The move was followed quickly by a 25 basis-point rise in the territory's prime lending rates to 8.75 percent, which bankers said could marginally affect the property market.
